**Abstract**

Natural language call routing can be treated as an instance of the topic categorization of documents after speech recognition of calls. This categorization consists of two important parts. The first part is text preprocessing, which is used to extract numerical data from the text. This is necessary because some information, such as prices or dates, may be useful for determining the category of the text. The second part of this process is classifying the text using machine learning techniques. Machine learning algorithms are good at classifying texts into categories, even when the number of categories is large. We use different kinds of algorithms to test them on our dataset, and we show that it's possible to route calls correctly most of the time, even when the number of categories (different topics) is large.

However, the study also shows that using internal procurement route would have no effect on the cooperation between buyer and supplier. 

Research limitations/implications – While the results of this paper are promising, further research can be done to validate the results of this study by investigating the effects of procurement route on other factors such as relationship building, trust and cooperation.

**Abstract**

Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) mediate distinct biological responses by activating similar intracellular signaling pathways. It is not known if the specificity of the response is determined by qualitative or quantitative differences in signaling output. To address this question, we developed a novel method for coupling RTKs from different families to the epidermal growth factor receptor cytoplasmic domain and investigated their effects on cell fate determination. We found that each RTK activated the same downstream signaling pathway but generated distinct responses by changing either the level of activation of the pathway or its duration. Our results support the idea that the specificity of RTKs depends on their different ability to generate qualitatively different signals rather than just the quantitative difference in the same kind of signal. These findings provide important insight into how specificity is achieved in RTK-dependent signal transduction.

Background: Since the SAMMPRIS trial, aggressive medical management (AMM) with the use of dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel) and high dose statin therapy has been standard of care for patients with Intracranial Arterial Stenosis (ICAS). However, despite this, there is a subgroup of patients that continue to experience recurrent strokes despite undergoing AMM. The purpose of this study was to compare these patients with the patients who did not have recurrent strokes and evaluate any differences between the two groups.

Objective: To compare patients with intracranial artery stenosis who were treated with AMM, but continued to have recurrent strokes, to those who did not have recurrent strokes after being treated with AMM.

Methods: We reviewed 236 patients who had undergone endovascular stent treatment for an intracranial stenosis. Of these 236 patients, 197 patients were followed for at least 1 year. In this cohort, we found 48 patients that did not have a recurrent stroke, while 49 patients continued to have recurrent stroke despite AMM.

Results: After using univariable and multivariable analysis, we found that having an atherosclerotic lesion and having a large lumen diameter stenosis (<3mm) was a risk factor for recurrent stroke despite AMM. We did not find significant differences in blood pressure, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, or smoking status between these two groups.

Conclusions: We conclude that in our patient population, the size of the atherosclerotic plaque, and its location, seems to be an important factor in determining if a patient will be free from recurrent stroke after being treated with AMM, while the usual other known risk factors for stroke do not seem as predictive in this study.
